# Coding

Coding owns project selection, conversations, coding rounds and durable command receipts. Web and external editors are peer clients of its single command boundary; each client owns its selection and drafts. The module exposes the owner-visible `command({input:string})` tool and `/api/coding` HTTP listener. Routed applications retain their actual caller identity. Coding calls the kernel as Coding and accepts no caller-supplied principal or Agent target.

See [protocol.md](./protocol.md) for commands, fields, receipts and responses. `handleCodingCommand(context, raw)` in `service.ts` serves both tool and HTTP paths using strict bounded commands. POST `/api/coding/v1/commands` receives command JSON and returns `{result: handlerOutput}`. Routed `chrona.call("coding.command", {input: JSON.stringify(command)})` returns `handlerOutput` directly.

The entry uses Coding's `client.ts` to call the kernel string targets `agent.run`, `agent.read`, `agent.write` and `agent.stop`. It has no dependency on an application named Agent. All mutation keys go in the third call options argument. Generic run arguments contain the prompt, optional context ID, `kind:"conversation"` and `providerOptions:{}`. Coding's work IDs, project references, start budgets and workflow fields stay in its own journal. The kernel governs execution budgets. Coding currently has no completion caller; a future one must use `run` with `kind:"completion"` and Provider options followed by `read`.

Projects are a Coding-owned registry of at most 100 canonical existing directories. Registering validates and resolves an absolute directory path; symlinks to the same directory share its project reference. Project selection becomes explicit task data in the prompt, with instructions to read applicable AGENTS.md rules and use explicit paths. It does not set kernel cwd, configure the Provider or grant filesystem authority. `projects.create` reports `unsupported` because no Coding-owned project creation root is configured. A conversation stays bound to one registered project.

Sending during a running round uses generic `write` with `input.kind:"message"`. Answering uses `input.kind:"answer"`, the original question ID and a typed Provider answer. Answers validate the current conversation, run, context, question status and expiry. Sending after terminal status and confirmed stop starts a new run with the previous `contextId`. The app's execution `sessionId` maps to kernel `contextId`; `attemptId` maps to kernel `runId`. These are distinct from the Coding conversation ID.

Local conversation creation and default-project changes save accepted receipts and state in one atomic journal replacement. External mutations persist their pending intent before dispatch. Duplicate identical commands return the stored receipt; changed arguments conflict. Explicit `round.retry` recovers the original target/key through `callStatus`. A missing or unavailable original receipt remains pending and never resubmits the mutation. Reads never dispatch another turn. There is no background retry loop or second execution queue.

Stop requests persist `cancelRequested` before dispatch. A successful request does not imply confirmed stop. After `stopConfirmed:false`, even a subsequent inactive terminal read cannot authorize continuation; a later explicit stop must supply confirmation. Unknown admission and unconfirmed stops block advancement.

Private storage uses fsynced atomic writes:

- `<data>/sessions/index.json`: version 2 conversations, current rounds, default project preference, original commands and public receipts. Limits are 1,000 conversations, 10,000 receipts and 64 MiB, with explicit capacity errors.
- `<data>/sessions/projects.json`: Coding's canonical project registry.
- `<data>/sessions/call-<sha256>.json`: original kernel target, options key, arguments, business binding and mutation outcome; bounded to 8 MiB per file.
- `<data>/sessions/run-<sha256>.json`: business work to kernel run/context binding, transcript time boundaries and stop evidence.
- `<data>/sessions/history-<workId>.json`: acquired transcript text, opaque event cursor, bounded snapshot and progress. Replies are cached up to 8 MiB encoded text and paged at 96 KiB in conversation responses. Snapshots truncate at 24,000 characters and mark missing/truncated evidence. Transcript retention limits, unprojected events and missing text remain explicit.
- `<data>/<workId>.json`: original start intent, fixed execution identity, result and acceptance records.

The generic kernel contract supplies no project/workspace placement, Git baseline, trusted diff or cleanup receipt. Those operations report `unsupported`; Coding does not manufacture result evidence or simulate workspaces. The existing immutable result reader/acceptance logic remains scoped to conversation → work → result, but new baseline-backed result capture cannot complete without a separate genuine application-owned source. Acceptance never applies a patch, commits, merges, pushes or deploys.

All encoded responses, including JSON escaping, base64 and transport envelopes, fit within 230 KiB. Oversized reads fail with `too_large`; oversized conversation snapshots are explicitly omitted. Output validation runs after durable mutation settlement and cannot change accepted receipts. Usage events are projected when their actual normalized payload matches; other events mark a gap rather than being invented as business events. Opaque kernel cursors are preserved unchanged.

`service.bun.test.ts` uses fresh temporary files and strict fake seven-tool schemas to cover concurrent clients, receipts, lost replies, restart recovery, stop fences, continuation, question identity/expiry, canonical projects, complete long reply pagination and response bounds. `entry.bun.test.ts` runs the shipped author tests through the offline SDK harness; `test.ts` exercises actual tool and HTTP entries with fake kernel stubs. `http.bun.test.ts` tests the HTTP adapter separately. No real model, account, user project or external service is used.

Run `bun packages/engine/src/modules/steward/external/coding/build-kernel.ts` to regenerate private kernel schemas and the distributed shared client copy. Coding's entry uses its own client so shared entry generation cannot restore application-based Agent addressing. The bundled `contract.js` contains private Coding workflow schemas, not additional kernel APIs. DAG/work-v2 helpers are not exposed by the command boundary or manifest and reject execution requiring unavailable workspace evidence. The legacy `page.ts` and `components.ts` remain unimported by the Coding entry. Coding registers no Web page, health hook, schedule or reconciliation tool.
